title: Design a URL Shortener
answer: Generate a unique key, store its mapping to the long URL durably, and keep redirects fast with a cache for popular keys. Record click analytics asynchronously so tracking does not slow the redirect path.
focus: Estimate a read-heavy workload, then decide what to cache and how to count clicks without slowing redirects.

title: Design an API Rate Limiter
answer: A token bucket handles bursts while enforcing an average refill rate. A strict global limit needs shared state across servers; local counters are more available but can temporarily exceed the intended limit.
focus: Compare counter and token-bucket designs, then decide how multiple servers share limits.

title: Design a News Feed (Twitter Timeline)
answer: Build most feeds by writing new posts into followers’ timelines, then fetch posts on read for very large publishers. A hybrid avoids making celebrity posts fan out to millions of inboxes while keeping ordinary reads fast.
focus: Choose between write fan-out and read fan-out when a few accounts have millions of followers.

title: Design an Uber-Style Ride-Sharing System
answer: Use a short-lived spatial index to find fresh, available drivers near a pickup, then rank a small candidate set by road ETA. Reserve the driver and ride with a conditional, versioned state transition before sending an offer; leases and idempotent replies make retries safe.
focus: Design Uber-style dispatch: match nearby drivers quickly without stale locations or double assignments, then isolate a stadium hotspot.

title: Design a Payment System
answer: Give each payment attempt a durable idempotency key and move it through an explicit state machine. Retries can then return the existing result, while provider events are deduplicated and reconciled instead of assuming exactly-once delivery.
focus: Make retries safe when a payment succeeds but the caller never receives the response.

title: Design a Distributed Job Queue
answer: Assume at-least-once delivery: acknowledge work only after its effect is durable, make handlers idempotent, and use expiring leases so another worker can recover a crashed job. Bound retries and route repeatedly failing jobs to a dead-letter queue.
focus: Handle duplicate delivery, worker crashes, retries and messages that can never succeed.

title: Design a Video Processing Pipeline
answer: Upload video bytes directly and resumably to object storage, while a durable state machine tracks each video and transcode job. Workers claim jobs with expiring, fenced leases and write attempt-specific outputs, so a crash can trigger a retry without letting stale work overwrite the current result.
focus: Separate upload, durable job state and transcoding so each can recover from failures independently.

title: Design a Dropbox-Style File Sync Service
answer: Split files into verified immutable blocks and publish versions through conditional metadata manifests. Let devices recover from an ordered change journal using durable cursors; preserve concurrent offline edits as conflict copies, authorize block reads against current permissions, and garbage-collect unreferenced blocks only after a safety delay.
focus: Keep large uploads resumable and file versions complete while devices reconnect, conflict, lose access and restore deleted data.

title: Design a Product Analytics System
answer: Append validated events to a durable stream before acknowledging them, then batch them into a column store for queries by team, event and time. Stable event IDs make retries safe; an identity override table handles anonymous-to-known user merges without rewriting the event history.
focus: Keep ingestion durable and deduplicated while making time-range analytics fast for each customer.

title: Design a Notification System
answer: Write product events through an outbox, then create notifications with stable deduplication keys. Delivery workers claim each notification through a state machine, recheck current preferences before sending, and isolate critical traffic from bulk traffic; retries must account for providers that may accept a message before timing out.
focus: Prevent duplicate sends, honor preference changes and protect urgent messages when a provider slows down.

title: Design a Distributed Cache (Memcache)
answer: Keep the database authoritative and treat the cache as a disposable, demand-filled copy. Record invalidations with each database commit and deliver them after replication; use leases to stop an old read from restoring stale data, and a spare pool to absorb a cache-node failure.
focus: Control stale reads and database load during writes, hot-key bursts and cache failures.

title: Design Discord's Message Storage
answer: Partition messages by channel and time bucket, then order them with time-sortable IDs so recent pages and history reads touch a small range. A routing layer keeps each channel’s reads local and coalesces identical requests; tombstones, repair and dual writes make deletes and live database moves explicit.
focus: Make channel history cheap to read while keeping hot channels and database migrations manageable.

title: Design a Collaborative Editor (Google Docs)
answer: Give each document one fenced owner to assign durable sequence numbers, while clients apply edits locally and resend unacknowledged operations after reconnecting. Use an operation merge algorithm so concurrent edits converge; keep transient presence separate from the durable edit log.
focus: Preserve one document history through concurrent edits, reconnects, owner changes and fan-out.

title: Design a Reactive Database (Live Queries)
answer: Run each query at a versioned snapshot and record the index ranges it reads. When a commit changes one of those ranges, rerun only the affected queries and push results with the commit timestamp; clients apply updates only when their subscriptions agree on that timestamp.
focus: Update subscribed query results without polling or showing data from mixed snapshots.

title: Shard a Live Database Without Downtime
answer: Shard by workspace because most reads and joins stay within one workspace, and map a fixed set of logical shards to database hosts. For migration, log writes, backfill versioned rows, catch up, verify with comparisons and dark reads, then cut over reversibly; handle cross-workspace features as a separate design problem.
focus: Scale write volume without rehashing every row, and migrate live data without losing newer writes.
